t: How to Navigate and Configure Thrive Apprentice Settings
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to navigate the Thrive Apprentice Settings page, configure general settings for your online school, and customize dynamic labels to match your brand's voice.

Accessing the Settings Page

To open the settings area, navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and click Settings in the left sidebar. This takes you to a centralized hub where you can manage every aspect of your online school's configuration.

Understanding the Settings Page Layout

The Settings page is organized into clearly labeled sections, each dedicated to a specific area of your Thrive Apprentice setup. You'll find the following tabs along the top or in the left-hand navigation:

  • General — Core settings such as your course page, URL slugs, auto-login, and comment preferences.
  • Login & Access Restriction — Controls for login pages, registration, and who can view your content.
  • Comments — Enable or disable comments on courses, lessons, and modules.
  • Email Templates — Customize automated emails sent to students upon enrollment, completion, and other events.
  • Assessment Uploads — Manage settings for student assignment submissions.
  • Labels & Translations — Adjust the default text and dynamic labels displayed throughout your courses.

Tip: You can jump directly to any section by clicking its name in the navigation. Each section saves independently, so you don't need to configure everything at once.

Configuring General Settings

The General tab is where you set the foundational options for your online school. Here's what you can configure:

Course Page Selection

Choose which WordPress page displays your Thrive Apprentice course catalog. This is the page visitors see when they browse all available courses on your site.

  1. Open the General settings tab.
  2. Locate the Course Page dropdown.
  3. Select the page you want to use as your main course listing page.
  4. Click Save to apply the change.

URL Slugs

Customize the URL structure for your courses, lessons, and modules. Clean, descriptive slugs improve both SEO and user experience.

  1. Scroll to the URL Slugs section in the General tab.
  2. Enter your preferred slug for each content type (e.g., courses, lessons).
  3. Click Save to update the URLs.

Important: Changing URL slugs after your site is live may break existing links. If you update slugs, set up 301 redirects for any previously shared URLs.

Auto-Login

When enabled, the Auto-login feature automatically logs users in when a new WordPress account is created for them. This provides a seamless experience for students who are added to your site through integrations or manual account creation.

  1. In the General tab, find the Auto-login toggle.
  2. Switch it On to enable automatic login for new accounts.
  3. Click Save.

Course Comments

You can enable or disable comments on your course content directly from the General tab. This lets students ask questions and interact with your material.

  1. Locate the Enable Comments for Courses option.
  2. Toggle it On or Off based on your preference.
  3. Click Save.

Using Dynamic Labels

Dynamic labels are adaptive text elements that automatically change based on the visitor's access status and context. For example, a label might display "Start Course" for a student with access and "Purchase Course" for someone who hasn't enrolled yet.

Where to Find Dynamic Labels

  1. Go to Settings > Labels & Translations.
  2. Select the Access Restrictions section.
  3. You'll see a list of customizable labels and call-to-action buttons on the right side of the screen.

Customizing Dynamic Labels

Each label corresponds to a specific scenario—such as free access, paid enrollment, or restricted content. To customize a label:

  1. Click on the label text you want to edit.
  2. Type your new text in the field provided.
  3. Repeat for any additional labels or call-to-action buttons.
  4. Click Save to apply your changes.

Here are some common labels you can adjust:

  • Free course label — Tells visitors the course is available at no cost.
  • Paid course label — Indicates that a purchase or subscription is required.
  • Call-to-action button text — The button text that prompts users to enroll, purchase, or log in.
  • Restricted content message — The message shown when a visitor cannot access course material.

Tip: Use clear, action-oriented language in your labels. Instead of generic text like "Access," try something more specific like "Enroll Now—It's Free!" or "Unlock This Course."

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to navigate the Thrive Apprentice Settings page, configure your general settings, and customize dynamic labels. With these fundamentals in place, your online school is ready for further customization.

t: How to Set Up Login, Registration, and Access Restrictions
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to configure login and registration pages, set up access restriction rules, manage what non-logged-in visitors see when they encounter restricted content, and register new users in Thrive Apprentice.

Prerequisites

  • At least one course created in Thrive Apprentice.
  • At least one product set up, since access restrictions are applied at the product level.

Understanding How Access Restrictions Work

Access restrictions in Thrive Apprentice operate at the product level, not at the individual course level. You create products that contain one or more courses, then apply restriction rules to those products. This approach gives you flexible control—you can bundle multiple courses into a single product and manage access for all of them at once.

When a visitor tries to access a course or lesson they don't have permission to view, Thrive Apprentice displays a customizable message based on the restriction settings you've configured. The Login & Access Restriction settings apply globally to all Thrive Apprentice products on your website.

Setting Up a Login and Registration Page

A dedicated login and registration page gives your students a clear entry point to access course content. Here's how to set one up:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Login & Access Restriction tab.
  4. In the Login Page section, click Add a Login Page (or select an existing page from the dropdown).
  5. Customize your login page settings—including form fields, branding, and redirect behavior.
  6. In the Registration section, enable registration if you want new users to create accounts on their own.
  7. Configure registration fields and any welcome email preferences.
  8. Click Save to apply your changes.

Tip: Use the Thrive Architect visual editor to design a professional-looking login and registration page that matches your site's branding.

Configuring Access Restriction Rules

Access restriction rules determine who can view your course content. You can restrict access so that only subscribers, purchasers, or specific user roles can access your products.

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Settings.
  2. Open the Login & Access Restriction tab.
  3. Scroll to the Access Restriction Rules section.
  4. Choose how you want to restrict content. Common options include:
  • Logged-in users only — Only users with a WordPress account can view the content.
  • Product purchasers — Only users who have purchased or been granted access to a specific product.
  • Specific user roles — Restrict access based on WordPress user roles such as Subscriber, Customer, or a custom role.
  1. Configure the restriction message that visitors see when they don't have access. This message can include a link to your login or purchase page.
  2. Click Save to apply the rules.

Note: These global restriction rules apply to all products. If you need different rules for individual products, you can override them at the product level by navigating to the specific product's settings.

What Non-Logged-In Users See

When a visitor who isn't logged in—or doesn't have the right permissions—tries to access restricted content, Thrive Apprentice shows them a restriction message. You have full control over what this message says and where it directs the visitor.

To customize the restriction message:

  1. Open Settings > Login & Access Restriction.
  2. Locate the Restricted Content Message area.
  3. Edit the text to communicate what the visitor needs to do—whether that's logging in, registering, or purchasing access.
  4. Optionally, include a link or button that directs visitors to your login page, registration form, or sales page.
  5. Click Save.

Tip: Keep your restriction message helpful rather than generic. Instead of "Access denied," try something like "This course is available to members. Log in or sign up to get started!"

Registering New Users

There are two primary ways to register new learners in Thrive Apprentice:

Self-Registration

When registration is enabled, visitors can sign up directly from your login/registration page. After registering, they receive a welcome email with their login credentials and can immediately begin accessing any courses included in their product access.

  1. Ensure registration is enabled under Settings > Login & Access Restriction.
  2. Verify that your registration page is published and accessible.
  3. When a visitor registers, Thrive Apprentice creates a new WordPress user account for them.
  4. The new user receives a welcome email with their login details.

Manually Granting Access

As an administrator, you can also manually add users and grant them access to specific products:

  1. Go to the Members section in Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Add Member or locate an existing WordPress user.
  3. Select the products you want to grant them access to.
  4. Save the changes. The user now has access to all courses within those products.

Important: When you grant access manually, the user must already have a WordPress account. If they don't, create one first under Users > Add New in your WordPress admin dashboard.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully set up login and registration pages, configured access restriction rules, customized restriction messages, and learned how to register new users. Your Thrive Apprentice courses are now properly secured and accessible to the right audience.

t: How to Manage Course Status and Bulk Actions
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to manage course statuses in Thrive Apprentice—including publishing, hiding, archiving, and scheduling courses—as well as how to use bulk actions to manage multiple courses at once.

Understanding Course Status Options

Every course in Thrive Apprentice has a status that controls its visibility and accessibility. Here are the available statuses:

  • Published — The course is live and visible to all visitors on your site. Students with access can enroll and start learning.
  • Draft — The course is not visible to anyone except administrators. Use this status while you're still building or editing your course content.
  • Hidden — The course is not listed publicly, but users with a direct link can still access it. This is ideal for exclusive or invite-only courses.
  • Archived — The course is removed from public listings and is no longer accessible to new students. Existing students who previously had access may still see it depending on your configuration.
  • Scheduled — The course is set to publish automatically at a specific date and time in the future.

How to Change a Course's Status

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar to view your course list.
  3. Hover over the course you want to modify.
  4. Click the status indicator or select Edit to open the course settings.
  5. Locate the Status dropdown and choose the desired status: Published, Draft, Hidden, Archived, or Scheduled.
  6. Click Save to apply the change.

Note: Changing a course from Published to Draft or Archived immediately removes it from public view. Students currently in the middle of a lesson won't be interrupted, but they won't be able to navigate to the course from the course listing page.

Scheduling a Course for Future Publication

The scheduling feature lets you set a course—or individual modules and lessons—to publish automatically at a specific date and time. This is perfect for drip content strategies or coordinated launch events.

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and open the course you want to schedule.
  2. Click the Content tab to view all modules and lessons.
  3. Hover over the Publish icon next to the lesson or module you want to schedule.
  4. Select Schedule from the options that appear.
  5. Set the date and time you want the content to go live.
  6. Click Save to confirm the schedule.

Once the scheduled date arrives, Thrive Apprentice automatically publishes the content—no manual action required on your part.

Tip: Scheduling works at both the course and lesson level. You can publish a course immediately while scheduling individual lessons to release over time—a great approach for drip-feeding content to your students.

Hiding Premium Courses from the Course List

If you offer premium courses that should only be visible to specific users or members, you can hide them from the public course list. This keeps your premium content exclusive while still allowing authorized users to access it via a direct link or through their member dashboard.

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Courses.
  2. Locate the premium course you want to hide.
  3. Change the course status to Hidden.
  4. Share the direct course URL only with authorized members or use your product access settings to control visibility.

Tip: Combine the Hidden status with product-level access restrictions for maximum control. Students who purchase or are granted access to the product will still see the course in their dashboard, even though it's hidden from the public listing.

Using Bulk Actions to Manage Multiple Courses

When you need to make changes to several courses at once, bulk actions save you significant time. Instead of editing each course individually, you can select multiple courses and apply changes in a single operation.

How to Use Bulk Actions

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Open the course you want to manage and click the Content tab.
  3. Select the checkboxes next to the lessons, modules, or chapters you want to modify.
  4. A Bulk Actions toolbar appears at the top of the content list.
  5. Choose the action you want to apply from the toolbar options.
  6. Confirm the action to apply it to all selected items.

Available Bulk Actions

  • Move — Relocate selected lessons or modules to a different chapter or position within the course.
  • Duplicate — Create copies of selected lessons or modules.
  • Delete — Remove selected items from the course.
  • Change status — Publish, unpublish, or schedule multiple items at once.

Important: Bulk delete is permanent. Double-check your selections before confirming a bulk delete action to avoid accidentally removing content you still need.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to manage course statuses, schedule future publications, hide premium courses, and use bulk actions to streamline your workflow. These tools give you complete control over how and when your course content appears to students.

t: How to Manage Members in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to use the Members section in Thrive Apprentice to view member details, track enrollment and progress, remove members, and import existing members from a CSV file.

Accessing the Members Section

The Members section provides a centralized view of everyone who has signed up for or purchased your courses. To access it:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Members in the left sidebar.

You'll see a dashboard listing all your Thrive Apprentice members. This is your command center for managing student access, tracking progress, and maintaining your membership base.

Understanding the Members Dashboard

The Members dashboard gives you a clear overview of your student base. Here's what you can find:

Engagement Summary

At the top of the page, the Engagement Summary displays key metrics through a set of cards. Use the filtering options to narrow down the data by date range or specific courses. These cards help you quickly assess overall member activity and engagement.

Member List

Below the summary, the member list shows each individual member with the following details:

  • Name and email — The member's identity and contact information.
  • Enrolled products — Which products (and their associated courses) the member has access to.
  • Progress — How far the member has advanced through their courses.
  • Status — Whether the member's access is active or has been revoked.

Tip: Use the search bar and filters at the top of the member list to quickly locate specific members by name, email, or product enrollment.

Managing Member Access

From the Members section, you can perform several key management actions for any individual member:

  • Grant access — Add a member to a product so they can access its courses.
  • Revoke access — Remove a member's access to a specific product without deleting their account.
  • Unlock or lock content — Control whether specific lessons or modules are available to a member.
  • View progress — Check how far the member has progressed through their enrolled courses.

To manage a specific member's access:

  1. Click on the member's name in the member list.
  2. Review their enrollment details and progress.
  3. Use the available options to grant, revoke, or modify their access.
  4. Click Save to apply any changes.

Removing Members

There are different levels of member removal depending on your needs. You can revoke product access while keeping the user account, or remove the member entirely from your system.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cv5FIGaKZ_Q

Revoking Product Access

If you only need to remove a member's access to specific courses—without deleting their WordPress account—use the revocation method:

  1. Go to Members in the left sidebar.
  2. Find the member in the list and click their name.
  3. Locate the product you want to revoke access for.
  4. Click Revoke Access next to the product.
  5. Confirm the action.

The member's WordPress account remains intact, but they will no longer be able to access the courses in that product.

Completely Removing a Member

To fully remove a member from Thrive Apprentice:

  1. Navigate to the Members section.
  2. Find and click the member you want to remove.
  3. Select the Remove option.
  4. Confirm the removal when prompted.

Important: Removing a member from Thrive Apprentice does not delete their WordPress user account. It only removes their Thrive Apprentice membership data. To delete the WordPress account entirely, go to Users in your WordPress admin dashboard.

Importing Existing Members

If you're migrating from another membership platform, you can import your existing members into Thrive Apprentice using a CSV file. This ensures a smooth transition without requiring each member to re-register.

Step 1: Export Your Member List

Most membership plugins allow you to export your member database as a .CSV file. Export your list from your previous platform, making sure it includes at minimum:

  • Email address (required)
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Any relevant membership or product information

Step 2: Import the CSV into Thrive Apprentice

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Members.
  2. Click the Import button at the top of the members list.
  3. Upload your .CSV file.
  4. Map the CSV columns to the corresponding Thrive Apprentice fields (e.g., email, first name, last name).
  5. Select which products the imported members should have access to.
  6. Click Import to begin the process.

Thrive Apprentice will create WordPress user accounts for any members who don't already have one and grant them access to the selected products.

Note: If a member's email address already matches an existing WordPress user, Thrive Apprentice will link the import to that existing account rather than creating a duplicate.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to access the Members dashboard, manage member access, remove members, and import existing members from a CSV file. With these tools, you can efficiently maintain your student base as your online school grows.
